class SQLResultHandler:
    def __init__(self, ...):
        ...
        self.related_model_meta = ...
    
    def next(self):
        data = self._fetch_next()
        if data is None:
            return None
        for i, (value, conversion) in enumerate(zip(data, self.converters)):
            if conversion is not None:
                value = conversion(value)
            data[i] = value
        related_populated = set()
        for i, (value, conversion) in enumerate(zip(data, self.converters)):
            if i in self.cols_order:
                field_num = self.cols_order[i]
                if field_num is None:
                    continue
                elif field_num not in self.related_populated:
                    ...
        ...

    def get_select_related(self):
        field_dict = {}
        if not self.select_related:
            return field_dict

        direct_select_related = {}
        related_fields = []
        # We need to deduplicate the paths from each other, so we'll build up
        # a dict by path.
        for name in self.select_related:
            if LOOKUP_SEP not in name:
                direct_select_related[name] = None
            else:
                relation, *rest = name.split(LOOKUP_SEP)
                field_dict[relation] = rest
                related_fields.append(relation)
        for relation in related_fields:
            if relation not in field_dict:
                field_dict[relation] = None
            elif isinstance(field_dict[relation], (list, tuple)):
                field_dict[relation] = tuple(
                    set(field_dict[relation]) | set(direct_select_related)
                )
        for relation, field_names in direct_select_related.items():
            field_dict.setdefault(relation, field_names)
        return field_dict
```

        field_dict = {}

        related_fields = []
        # We need to deduplicate the paths from each other, so we'll build up
        # a dict by path.

            if LOOKUP_SEP not in name:
                direct_select_related[name] = None

                relation, *rest = name.split(LOOKUP_SEP)

                related_fields.append(relation)

                field_dict[relation] = None
            elif isinstance(field_dict[relation], (list, tuple)):
                field_dict[relation] = tuple(
                    set(field_dict[relation]) | set(direct_select_related)
                )
        for relation, field_names in direct_select_related.items():
            field_dict.setdefault(relation, field_names)

Let me remember the real code (Django 4.2) `SQLCompiler.get_related_selections`:

```python
    def get_related_selections(self):
        related_selections = super().get_related_selections()
        for parent_alias, field_iter in (
            self.query.get_select_related().items()
        ):
            if parent_alias is None:
                # The model itself wasn't deferred
                only_deferred = False
            else:
                # The parent model instance was fetched fully.
                # This can be true in two cases:
                #  1. When the parent model comes from a table without
                #     any deferral-related clauses (SELECT *, SELECT DISTINCT,
                #     having columns in GROUP BY, etc.)
                #  2. When the parent model's table is appearing again
                #     after previously having all of its columns.
                model = self.query.model
                parent_fields = {
                    field
                    for field in model._meta.concrete_fields
                    if field.column in self.get_original_columns(...)
                }

```python
    def get_related_selections(self):
        """
        Compute the columns and joins needed for related selections
        without any column aliasing.
        """
        query = self.query
        select = query.select
        related_selections = []
        for name, field_iter in query.get_select_related().items():
            model = select[0].model
            join_infos = []
            for field in field_iter:
                try:
                    join_info = query.setup_joins([field], model, self.alias_refcounter)
                    final_field = join_info.joins[-1].target_final_field
                    model = final_field.model
                except FieldDoesNotExist:
                    # No join required.
                    final_field = None
                join_infos.append(final_field)
                for join in join_info.joins:
                    related_selections.append(join.table_name)
            related_selections.append(model)
        return related_selections
```

```python
    def get_select_related(self):
        field_dict = {}
        if not self.select_related:
            return field_dict

        direct_select_related = {}
        related_fields = []
        # We need to deduplicate the paths from each other, so we'll build up
        # a dict by path.
        for name in self.select_related:
            if LOOKUP_SEP not in name:
                direct_select_related[name] = None
            else:
                relation, *rest = name.split(LOOKUP_SEP)
                field_dict[relation] = rest
                related_fields.append(relation)
        for relation in related_fields:
            if relation not in field_dict:
                field_dict[relation] = None
            elif isinstance(field_dict[relation], (list, tuple)):
                field_dict[relation] = tuple(
                    set(field_dict[relation]) | set(direct_select_related)
                )
        for relation, field_names in direct_select_related.items():
            field_dict.setdefault(relation, field_names)
        return field_dict
```

```python
def select_related(self, *fields):
    if not fields:
        raise TypeError("No related fields (provide at least one)")
    clone = self._chain()
    clone.query.select_related = True if not fields else clone.query.select_related | set(fields)
    return clone
```

```python
def _setup_joins(self, optname, opts, alias, join_list):
    """
    Compute the TableJoin instances needed to reach 'optname' starting from
    the table 'alias'. The optname is a path of relations name in the model.
    """
    join_names, final_rel = optname.split(LOOKUP_SEP), None
    joins, alias, rel_obj = self._traverse_join(
        optname,
        opts,
        alias,
        join_list,
        can_reuse=set(),
        fail_on_missing=True,
    )
    join_list.extend(joins)
    return [j.table_alias for j in joins], final_rel
```

def get_field(self, field_name):
    """
    Return a field instance given the name of a forward or reverse field.
    """
    try:
        field = getattr(self.model, field_name)
    except AttributeError:
        field = getattr(self, field_name)
    except (AttributeError, TypeError):
        # for non-relatable field names or missing related fields
        # e.g. 'foo' or 'foo__bar'
        # raise FieldDoesNotExist
        for model in self.get_fields()...
```

Let me think about what select_related does for a FilteredRelation in the compiler's `get_related_selections`:

```python
for name in list(requested):
    # Filtered relations work only on the topmost level.
    if cur_depth > 1:
        break
    if name in self.query._filtered_relations:
        fields_found.add(name)
        final_field, _, join_opts, joins, _, _ = self.query.setup_joins(
            [name], opts, root_alias
        )
        model = join_opts.model
        alias = joins[-1]
        from_parent = (
            issubclass(model, opts.model) and model is not opts.model
        )
        klass_info = {
            "model": model,
            "field": final_field,
            "reverse": True,
            "local_setter": partial(local_setter, final_field),
            "remote_setter": partial(remote_setter, name),
            "from_parent": from_parent,
        }
```

if name in self._filtered_relations and pos == 0:

def names_to_path(self, names, opts, allow_many=True, fail_on_missing=False):
    """
    ...
    """
    path, names_with_path = [], []
    for pos, name in enumerate(names):
        cur_names_with_path = (name, [])
        if name == "pk":
            name = opts.pk.name

        field = None
        filtered_relation = None
        try:
            if opts is None:
                raise FieldDoesNotExist
            field = opts.get_field(name)
        except FieldDoesNotExist:
            if name in self.annotation_select:
                field = self.annotation_select[name].output_field
            elif name in self._filtered_relations and pos == 0:
                filtered_relation = self._filtered_relations[name]
                if LOOKUP_SEP in filtered_relation.relation_name:
                    parts = filtered_relation.relation_name.split(LOOKUP_SEP)
                    filtered_relation_path, field, _, _ = self.names_to_path(
                        parts,
                        opts,
                        allow_many,
                        fail_on_missing,
                    )
                    path.extend(filtered_relation_path[:-1])
                else:
                    field = opts.get_field(filtered_relation.relation_name)
```

SQL generated:
```sql
SELECT ps.id, ps.name, ps.pool_id, ps.another_pool_id,
       T4.id, T4.name, T4.tournament_id, T4.organiser_id
FROM poolstyle
INNER JOIN pool ON (ps.pool_id = pool.id)

from django.db.models.sql.query import Query
from django.db.models.sql.compiler import SQLCompiler

_o1 = F_.Field.set_cached_value
def p1(self, instance, value):
    print("SET Field.%s key=%s on %s(%s) <- %s(%s)" % (
        getattr(self,'name',self), self.get_cache_name(), type(instance).__name__, instance.pk,
        'None' if value is None else type(value).__name__, 'None' if value is None else value.pk))
    return _o1(self, instance, value)
F_.Field.set_cached_value = p1

_o2 = FR_.ForeignObjectRel.set_cached_value
def p2(self, instance, value):
    print("SET Rel(%s) key=%s on %s(%s) <- %s(%s)" % (
        str(self), self.get_cache_name(), type(instance).__name__, instance.pk,
        'None' if value is None else type(value).__name__, 'None' if value is None else value.pk))
    return _o2(self, instance, value)
FR_.ForeignObjectRel.set_cached_value = p2

_o3 = Query.setup_joins
def p3(self, names, opts, alias, *a, **k):
    r = _o3(self, names, opts, alias, *a, **k)
    ff, targets, jo, joins, path, tf = r
    if names and names[0] == 'tournament_pool':
        print("JOINS", names, "ff=", ff, type(ff).__name__, "to=", jo.model.__name__)
        for pi in path:
            fr = pi.filtered_relation
            print("   pi %s->%s direct=%s jf=%s fr_alias=%s" % (
                pi.from_opts.model.__name__, pi.to_opts.model.__name__, pi.direct,
                pi.join_field, fr.alias if fr else None))
    return r
Query.setup_joins = p3

_o4 = SQLCompiler.get_related_selections
def desc(f):
    if f is None: return 'None'
    if hasattr(f, 'func'): f = f.func
    return getattr(f, '__name__', repr(f))
def p4(self, *a, **k):
    r = _o4(self, *a, **k)
    for ki in r:
        print("KI model=%s field=%s rev=%s ls=%s rs=%s sub=%d" % (
            ki.get('model').__name__, ki.get('field'), ki.get('reverse'),
            desc(ki.get('local_setter')), desc(ki.get('remote_setter')),
            len(ki.get('related_klass_infos') or [])))
    return r
SQLCompiler.get_related_selections = p4

from known_related_objects.models import Organiser, Pool, PoolStyle, Tournament

with connection.schema_editor() as se:
    for m in (Tournament, Organiser, Pool, PoolStyle):
        se.create_model(m)

t1 = Tournament.objects.create(name="Tourney 1")
t2 = Tournament.objects.create(name="Tourney 2")
o1 = Organiser.objects.create(name="Organiser 1")
P1 = Pool.objects.create(name="T1 Pool 1", tournament=t1, organiser=o1)
P2 = Pool.objects.create(name="T1 Pool 2", tournament=t1, organiser=o1)
P3 = Pool.objects.create(name="T2 Pool 1", tournament=t2, organiser=o1)
P4 = Pool.objects.create(name="T2 Pool 2", tournament=t2, organiser=o1)
PoolStyle.objects.create(name="T1 Pool 2 Style", pool=P2)
PoolStyle.objects.create(name="T2 Pool 1 Style", pool=P3)
PoolStyle.objects.create(name="T1 Pool 1/3 Style", pool=P1, another_pool=P3)

qs = PoolStyle.objects.annotate(tournament_pool=FilteredRelation('pool__tournament__pool')).select_related('tournament_pool')

for i, row in enumerate(rows):

          "tc", {} if tp is None else {k: (type(v).__name__, v.pk) for k, v in tp._state.fields_cache.items()})

```python
for name in list(requested):
    # Filtered relations work only on the topmost level.
    if cur_depth > 1:
        break
    if name in self.query._filtered_relations:
        fields_found.add(name)
        final_field, _, join_opts, joins, _, _ = self.query.setup_joins(
            [name], opts, root_alias
        )
        model = join_opts.model
        alias = joins[-1]
        from_parent = (
            issubclass(model, opts.model) and model is not opts.model
        )
        klass_info = {
            "model": model,
            "field": final_field,
            "reverse": True,
            "local_setter": partial(local_setter, final_field),
            "remote_setter": partial(remote_setter, name),
            "from_parent": from_parent,
        }
```

    print("SET FK(%s.%s) on %s(%s) <- %s" % (type(instance).__name__, self.get_cache_name(), type(instance).__name__, instance.pk, value))

Query.setup_joins = p3

    """Get path from this field to the related model."""
    opts = self.remote_field.model._meta
    from_opts = self.model._meta
    return [
        PathInfo(
            from_opts=from_opts,
            to_opts=opts,
            target_fields=self.foreign_related_fields,
            join_field=self,
            m2m=False,
            direct=True,
            filtered_relation=filtered_relation,
        )

        if self.reorder_for_init:

        if obj is not None:

    def populate(self, row, from_obj):
        if self.reorder_for_init:
            obj_data = self.reorder_for_init(row)
        else:
            obj_data = row[self.cols_start : self.cols_end]
        if obj_data[self.pk_idx] is None:
            obj = None
        else:
            obj = self.model_cls.from_db(self.db, self.init_list, obj_data)
            for rel_iter in self.related_populators:
                rel_iter.populate(row, obj)
        self.local_setter(from_obj, obj)
        if obj is not None:
            self.remote_setter(obj, from_obj)
```

    def populate(self, row, from_obj):
        if self.reorder_for_init:
            obj_data = self.reorder_for_init(row)
        else:
            obj_data = row[self.cols_start : self.cols_end]
        if obj_data[self.pk_idx] is None:
            obj = None
        else:
            obj = self.model_cls.from_db(self.db, self.init_list, obj_data)
            for rel_iter in self.related_populators:
                rel_iter.populate(row, obj)
        self.local_setter(from_obj, obj)
        if obj is not None:
            self.remote_setter(obj, from_obj)
```

```python
    def populate(self, row, from_obj):
        if self.reorder_for_init:
            obj_data = self.reorder_for_init(row)
        else:
            obj_data = row[self.cols_start : self.cols_end]
        if obj_data[self.pk_idx] is None:
            obj = None
        else:
            obj = self.model_cls.from_db(self.db, self.init_list, obj_data)
            for rel_iter in self.related_populators:
                rel_iter.populate(row, obj)
        self.local_setter(from_obj, obj)
        if obj is not None:
            self.remote_setter(obj, from_obj)
```

Hmm, actually, the structure (Django 4.x) is:

```python
        for f in opts.fields:
            fields_found.add(f.name)

            if restricted:
                next = requested.get(f.name, {})
                if not f.is_relation:
                    # If a non-related field is used like a relation,
                    # or if a single non-relational field is given.
                    if next or f.name in requested:
                        raise FieldError(
                            "Invalid parameter name for %s.select_related(): %s "
                            "is not a relation." % (opts.model.__name__, f.name)
                        )
                    continue
                if not next and f.name not in requested:
                    # If this isn't the last part of the path, check that
                    # the field is a relation.
                    if cur_depth < max_depth:
                        if not f.related_fields:
                            raise FieldError(...)
                    continue
            else:
                next = {}
                if cur_depth == max_depth:
                    break
                if not f.related_fields:
                    continue
            # So far so good, at last let's check whether the field is going
            # to be related; but then only if select_related is not an empty
            # dict.

        def get_cache_name(self):

class ForeignObjectRel(FieldCacheMixin):
    ...
    def __init__(self, field, to, related_name=None, related_query_name=None, limit_choices_to=None, parent_link=False, on_delete=None):
        self.field = field

        # way around. We cache the children on the parent's using the field's

```python
    def populate(self, row, from_obj):
        if self.reorder_for_init:
            obj_data = self.reorder_for_init(row)
        else:
            obj_data = row[self.cols_start : self.cols_end]
        if obj_data[self.pk_idx] is None:
            obj = None
        else:
            obj = self.model_cls.from_db(self.db, self.init_list, obj_data)
            for rel_iter in self.related_populators:
                rel_iter.populate(row, obj)
        self.local_setter(from_obj, obj)
        if obj is not None:

ForeignObjectRel has:

```python
class ForeignObjectRel(FieldCacheMixin):
    """
    Used by the ForeignObject to store information about the relation.

    ``_meta.get_fields()`` returns this class to provide access to the field
    flags using the same API as for fields.

    ForeignObjectRel should be API compatible but have fewer options available.
    """

    field_class = None
    one_to_many = False
    one_to_one = False

    def __init__(self, field, to, related_name=None, ...):
        ...
        self.field = field

    def get_cache_name(self):
        """
        Which cache field to use for storing object instances in self.field's
        model.
        """
        return self.get_accessor_name()

    def set_cached_value(self, instance, value):
        setattr(instance, self.get_cache_name(), value)

    def get_cached_value(self, instance):
        return getattr(instance, self.get_cache_name())
```

And ManyToOneRel:

```python
class ManyToOneRel(ForeignObjectRel):
    one_to_many = True

    def __init__(self, field, to, field_name=None, related_name=None, ...):
        super().__init__(
            field,
            to,
            related_name=related_name,
            related_query_name=related_query_name,
            limit_choices_to=limit_choices_to,
            parent_link=parent_link,
            on_delete=on_delete,
        )
        self.field_name = field_name

    @property
    def target_field(self):
        # If the field that this relation targets is a concrete field on the
        # target model, return that field. Otherwise, find the concrete field
        # that this foreign key targets.
        target = self.field.model._meta.get_field(self.field_name)
        if not target.concrete:
            # If the target is not concrete, then this is a swappable error
            ...
            return self.field.model._meta.get_field(target.field_name)  # hmm, not exactly
        return target
```

```

```python
def get_field(self, field_name):
    """
    Return a field instance given the name of a forward or reverse field.
    """
    try:
        # In order to avoid premature loading of the relation tree
        # (expensive) we'll check whether we're looking at a forward field.
        return self._forward_fields_map[field_name]
    except KeyError:
        # next, try related objects
        for field in self.related_objects:
            if field.name == field_name:
                return field
        raise
```

Yes! `Tournament._meta.get_field('pool')` returns the ManyToOneRel `pool` (reverse of Pool.tournament). So `field` = ManyToOneRel. Then `pathinfos = field.get_path_info(filtered_relation)`.

class ForeignObjectRel(FieldCacheMixin):
    """
    Used by the ForeignObject to store information about the relation.

    ``_meta.get_fields()`` returns this class to provide access to the field
    flags using the same API as for fields.

    ForeignObjectRel should be API compatible but have fewer options available.
    """

    field_class = None
    one_to_many = False
    one_to_one = False

    def __init__(self, field, to, related_name=None, related_query_name=None, limit_choices_to=None, parent_link=False, on_delete=None):
        self.field = field
        self.model = to
        self.related_name = related_name
        self.related_query_name = related_query_name
        self.limit_choices_to = {} if limit_choices_to is None else limit_choices_to
        self.parent_link = parent_link
        self.on_delete = on_delete

        self.boolean = False

    def __str__(self):
        """
        Used as the name for the composite foreign key when it's applied as a
        query.
        """
        return "%s__%s" % (self.model._meta.label, self.field_name)

    def __repr__(self):
        """
        Used for the core object dispatcher.
        """
        return "%s (%s to %s)" % (
            self.__class__.__name__,
            self.field_name,
            self.model._meta.label,
        )

    def get_related_field(self):
        return self.field

    def get_cached_value(self, instance):
        ...
```

    """

        self.limit_choices_to = {} if limit_choices_to is None else limit_choices_to
        self.parent_link = parent_link
        self.on_delete = on_delete

        self.boolean = False

        ...

    def __repr__(self):
        ...

    def get_cached_value(self, instance):

```python
class OneToOneRel(ForeignObjectRel):
    """
    Used for the reverse relation of the OneToOneField.
    """

    field_class = OneToOneField
    one_to_many = False
    one_to_one = True

    def get_related_field(self):
        field = super().get_related_field()
        if field.attname != self.model._meta.pk.attname:
            return self.model._meta.pk
        return field

    def get_cache_name(self):
        # Use the name of the field pointing to the TO rather than the FROM.
        # We have to use this because it works on either side of a relation.
        return self.field.name

    def get_cached_value(self, instance):
        # The cached value is set when we're called from get_queryset()
        return instance._state.fields_cache[instance._meta.get_field(self.field_name)]

    def set_cached_value(self, instance, value):
        instance._state.fields_cache[instance._meta.get_field(self.field_name)] = value
```

Yes! OneToOneRel overrides get_cached_value/set_cached_value to use `instance._meta.get_field(self.field_name)` as the cache key! So for OneToOneRel of PoolStyle.pool (field_name='pool'), `set_cached_value(instance, value)` sets `instance._state.fields_cache[instance._meta.get_field('pool')] = value` — the cache key is the field on instance's own meta. So `OneToOneRel(poolstyle).set_cached_value(style, pool)`... would do style._meta.get_field('pool') = the PoolStyle.pool O2O field → sets style.pool cache = pool. Hmm interesting.

    def get_cached_value(self, instance):

```python
def select_related_descend(field, restricted, requested, select_mask, reverse=False):
    """
    Check whether a field should be descended into or not.

    :param field: the field describing the relation to descend
    :param restricted: a flag denoting whether select_related() was supplied
        with a list of field names.
    :param requested: A dictionary of levels at which the user requested data
        to be fetched, obtained by splitting the names in the select_related()
        call on '__'.
    :param select_mask: a dictionary specifying which fields should be fetched.
    :param reverse: A flag denoting whether the field is part of a reverse
        relation.
    """
    if field.name in requested:
        return True
    elif not restricted and not select_mask.get(field) and (
        # Check for m2m backref
        field.name
        or reverse
    ):
        return True
    elif not restricted:
        return bool(requested)
```

The related model's (to_opts side) field pointing to the from_opts model:
- If the hop is reverse (like our case): join_field = ManyToOneRel/OneToOneRel; the related model's field = `join_field.field` (the FK/O2O on the related model). Its name: 'tournament'.
- If the hop is direct: join_field = FK/O2O on the from model; the related model is the target; there's no field on the related model pointing back (except the reverse manager) → nothing to select (and not needed: the related object's "parent link" is an FK column already in the row... e.g., FR 'pool__tournament': T4→... wait, for that case, the related model = Tournament (B), already fully selected; Tournament has no FK back to Pool. Correct, nothing needed.)

So the rule: if the final hop is reverse, add a nested select_related of `join_field.field` (the FK on the related model) using alias joins[-2] (the final hop's parent's alias).

```python
class ForeignObjectRel(FieldCacheMixin):
    """
    Used by the ForeignObject to store information about the relation.

    ``_meta.get_fields()`` returns this class to provide access to the field
    flags using the same API as for fields.

    ForeignObjectRel should be API compatible but have fewer options available.
    """

    field_class = None
    one_to_many = False
    one_to_one = False

    def __init__(self, field, to, related_name=None, related_query_name=None, limit_choices_to=None, parent_link=False, on_delete=None):
        self.field = field
        self.model = to
        self.related_name = related_name
        self.related_query_name = related_query_name
        self.limit_choices_to = {} if limit_choices_to is None else limit_choices_to
        self.parent_link = parent_link
        self.on_delete = on_delete

        self.boolean = False

    def __str__(self):
        """
        Used as the name for the composite foreign key when it's applied as a
        query.
        """
        return "%s__%s" % (self.model._meta.label, self.field_name)

    def __repr__(self):
        """
        Used for the core object dispatcher.
        """
        return "%s (%s to %s)" % (
            self.__class__.__name__,
            self.field_name,
            self.model._meta.label,
        )

    def get_related_field(self):
        return self.field

    def get_cached_value(self, instance):
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "Subclasses of ForeignObjectRel must override the get_cached_value()."
        )

    def set_cached_value(self, instance, value):
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "Subclasses of ForeignObjectRel must override the set_cached_value()."
        )

    def get_cache_name(self):
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "Subclasses of ForeignObjectRel must override get_cache_name()."
        )
```

    def join(self, join, reuse=None, reuse_with_filtered_relation=False):
        """
        Return an alias for the 'join' - a Join object or table name.

        If 'reuse' is given, it should be a set of alias keys which can be
        reused for this join. It will also be mutated in this method (either
        removing elements which were used, or adding the new alias if the join

And find_join:

```python
    def find_join(self, join, reuse=None):
        """
        Check whether a given join can be reused or not. Return the alias if it
        can, None otherwise. 'join' is a Join instance, 'reuse' a set of
        aliases which can be reused.

        Note that the found join might not be usable in case the query has a
        WHERE condition on the join and it is not reusable.
        """
        # Check if the join can be reused
        conditions = join.join_on()
        # Note that we will be muting the reuse parameter.
        # Do not abuse it!
        if reuse is not None:
            for alias in reuse:
                if alias in self.alias_map:
                    existing = self.alias_map[alias]
                    # Don't reuse the same alias with a different join type.
                    if existing.join_type != join.join_type:
                        continue
                    if not conditions == existing.join_on():
                        continue
                    return alias
        else:
            for alias, potential_reuse in self.alias_map.items():
                if isinstance(potential_reuse, self.alias_refcount.__class__):
                    continue
                if not conditions == potential_reuse.join_on():
                    continue
                if not (isinstance(potential_reuse, Join) and potential_reuse.join_type == join.join_type):
                    continue
                return alias
```

Actually! I remember: `ForeignObjectRel` is in `django/db/models/fields/related.py`:

```python
class ForeignObjectRel(FieldCacheMixin):
    """
    Used by ForeignObject to store information about the relation.

    ``_meta.get_fields()`` returns this class to provide access to the field
    flags for the reverse relation.
    """

    # Field flags
    auto_created = True
    concrete = False
    editable = False
    is_relation = True

    # Reverse relations are never nullable to the same value as the forward
    # relation.
    # For example, `class State(Country)` doesn't produce a
    # nullable reverse relation to State, even if the forward relation is
    # nullable.
    null = False
    empty_strings_allowed = False

        self,
        field,
        to,
        related_name=None,
        related_query_name=None,
        limit_choices_to=None,
        parent_link=False,
        on_delete=None,
    ):
        self.field = field
        self.model = to
        self.related_name = related_name
        self.related_query_name = related_query_name
        self.limit_choices_to = {} if limit_choices_to is None else limit_choices_to
        self.parent_link = parent_link
        self.on_delete = on_delete

    def __repr__(self):
        ...

        ...

Hmm, actually, wait a moment, let me look at `FieldCacheMixin`:

```python
class FieldCacheMixin:
    """Provide the default methods for managing model field cache."""

    def get_cache_name(self):
        return self.name

    def set_cached_value(self, instance, value):
        instance._state.fields_cache[self.get_cache_name()] = value

    def get_cached_value(self, instance, default=None):
        return instance._state.fields_cache.get(self.get_cache_name(), default)

    def is_cached(self, instance):
        return self.get_cache_name() in instance._state.fields_cache

    def remove_cached_value(self, instance):
        del instance._state.fields_cache[self.get_cache_name()]
```

This is what FK fields and rels use. So `rel.set_cached_value(instance, value)` → `instance._state.fields_cache[rel.get_cache_name()] = value`.

For the corruption `Pool(1)._state.fields_cache['tournament'] = style1`, the caller must have been an object with set_cached_value(P1, style1) and get_cache_name()=='tournament'. 3 queries: (1) main query, (2) `p[0].pool` (style.pool is not select_related'd... wait, only 'tournament_pool' is select_related'd), (3) `.pool.tournament`. Then `p[0].tournament_pool.tournament` must be a cache hit — meaning tournament_pool (Pool P1) needs to have its tournament cache correctly set to Tournament t1.

How do we get P1.tournament = t1 without an extra query? The SELECT has columns for T4 (Pool) only: T4.id, T4.name, T4.tournament_id, T4.organiser_id. We don't SELECT Tournament. So to have P1.tournament cached as a Tournament object, we'd need the intermediate Tournament's columns in the select... or we'd need to select_related a multi-level: `select_related('tournament_pool')` where the FR path is pool→tournament→pool — the "related model" is Pool, reached via tournament. In standard select_related semantics for `style__pool__tournament`... wait, the root is PoolStyle; the FR 'pool__tournament__pool' from PoolStyle leads to a Pool. So the select_related('tournament_pool') is analogous to select_related('pool__tournament') — 2 levels! In the normal select_related('pool__tournament') case, Django would select Pool and Tournament, cache style.pool, pool.tournament, tournament.poolstyle.

So the correct behavior: the klass_info for tournament_pool should include the intermediate Tournament as a nested related_klass_info, so that:
- style.tournament_pool = P_i (Pool),
- P_i.tournament = T (Tournament) — cached correctly,
- (and T's reverse... probably not needed).

But the SQL SELECT currently only selects T4's columns (Pool). It doesn't SELECT tournament's columns! Looking at the SQL:

```
SELECT "known_related_objects_poolstyle"."id", ..., T4."id", T4."name", T4."tournament_id", T4."organiser_id"
FROM poolstyle
INNER JOIN pool ON (poolstyle.pool_id = pool.id)
INNER JOIN tournament ON (pool.tournament_id = tournament.id)
LEFT OUTER JOIN pool T4 ON (tournament.id = T4.tournament_id)
```

So tournament's columns aren't selected. The joins are: poolstyle → pool (INNER) → tournament (INNER) → T4 (LEFT OUTER).

To cache P_i.tournament = Tournament(t1), we need Tournament's columns in the SELECT. Options:

Option A: change get_related_selections to add the intermediate columns (like a nested related_klass_info). That changes the SQL — select tournament's columns too. Then queries: main(1) + style.pool lazy(2) + pool.tournament lazy(3) + tp.tournament cache hit. Total 3.

Option B: don't cache the back-reference at all for multi-level (skip local_setter), so `tp.tournament` lazy-loads → 4 queries → test fails (assertNumQueries(3)).

The test demands 3 queries, so Option A (selecting the intermediate Tournament's columns and caching them correctly).

Hmm wait, but actually, wait. Let me reconsider: `p[0].pool.tournament` — p[0].pool is style.pool = P2 (lazy, query 2). P2.tournament = t1 (lazy, query 3). Then `p[0].tournament_pool` = P1 (already cached from select_related). `p[0].tournament_pool.tournament` must be cached → P1.tournament must be a cached Tournament t1.

So yes: the fix must ensure that when a multi-level FilteredRelation's final hop goes through an intermediate model, the intermediate object is also constructed and cached on the related object (like normal select_related descent).

So in get_related_selections' FR branch, instead of just doing setup_joins([name]) with a flat final_field, we need to descend the path. How does the normal (non-FR) multi-level select_related work? It recurses: for a field f (e.g., 'pool'), it creates a klass_info and recurses with `next = requested.get(f.name, {})`. The dict for requested['tournament_pool'] — how did it come there? From `add_select_related`: `field_dict = {}; for field in fields: for part in field.split(LOOKUP_SEP): d = d.setdefault(part, {})`. select_related('tournament_pool') → {'tournament_pool': {}}. So requested = {'tournament_pool': {}}.

For a normal 2-level 'pool__tournament', requested = {'pool': {'tournament': {}}}, and the recursion handles it.

For an FR, 'tournament_pool' is a top-level key in requested and handled in the FR branch. The FR branch calls setup_joins([name], ...) and creates a single klass_info with no nested klass_infos. To fix, the FR branch should process the path returned by setup_joins: the path has 3 PathInfos: PoolStyle.pool (direct), Pool.tournament (direct), reverse FK (with filtered_relation). The final field is the reverse ManyToOneRel.

Approach: for a multi-hop FR, we need to build nested klass_infos corresponding to the intermediate models, so that:
- level 1: Pool via style.pool (the first hop) — wait, but the first hop's alias is the INNER JOIN'd 'known_related_objects_pool' (alias 'pool' — the actual pool table joined). Hmm, but note: the first hop here is style.pool, which is a OneToOneField. In normal select_related('pool'), style.pool would be a direct field with local_setter = f.set_cached_value, etc.

But in the FR case, the first hop's pool is the style's own pool (INNER JOIN'd). If we select_related it, we cache style.pool — that's fine and correct. And the second hop: pool.tournament (FK) → cache pool.tournament = Tournament, and select Tournament's columns from alias 'known_related_objects_tournament'. And the third hop: the reverse FR hop → Pool T4, the main klass_info.

So the FR branch should:
1. Get the full path from setup_joins (already computed; unpack path — currently it's being discarded with `_`).
2. Build klass_infos for the intermediate models (path[:-1]) — for each hop in path[:-1], create a klass_info with the proper local/remote setters (like the normal branches), select columns from the appropriate alias, and nest them: style → (pool hop) → (tournament hop) → T4's klass_info.

- If len(path) == 1 (single hop): keep current behavior (local_setter with final_field).
- If len(path) > 1: build the intermediate klass_infos, so the intermediate objects are also selected and cached, and don't set the bogus reverse cache on the final object.

Building the intermediate chain: the chain is a linked list of models: root opts --PI1--> M1 (Pool) --PI2--> M2 (Tournament) --PI3--> M3 (Pool, final). What we need:
- style's related_klass_infos: [KI(M1)] where KI(M1) has related_klass_infos [KI(M2)], KI(M2) has [KI(M3)] (the final one).

We want pool cached on style: `PoolStyle.pool.set_cached_value(style, pool)` → style._state.fields_cache['pool'] = pool. In the normal forward branch: `"local_setter": f.set_cached_value` — populate: local_setter(from_obj=style, obj=pool) → f.set_cached_value(style, pool). Yes, so local_setter = PI1.join_field.set_cached_value (the actual field PoolStyle.pool).
- remote_setter for KI(M1): cache M1 back on style: if PI1 is a unique relation (O2O/FK): PI1.join_field.remote_field.set_cached_value(pool, style) → pool.poolstyle = style. In the normal forward branch: `"remote_setter": f.remote_field.set_cached_value if f.unique else lambda x, y: None`.
- KI(M2): join_field = Pool.tournament (FK). local: Pool.tournament.set_cached_value(pool_M1, tournament) → pool_M1.tournament = t1 ✓. remote: FK is not unique → lambda no-op.

Ah, here's the problem. In the nested populate: style's populator → KI(M1).populate(row, style) → creates pool_M1, then its related_populators: KI(M2).populate(row, pool_M1) → creates t1, then KI(M3).populate(row, t1) → creates T4, and remote_setter(T4, t1) → setattr(t1, 'tournament_pool', T4) — wrong! So the final remote_setter can't be a simple nested partial(remote_setter, name) — it needs to capture the root's from_obj. Hmm.

How does populate pass from_obj? RelatedPopulator.populate(row, from_obj): from_obj is the object owning the relation. Nested: each level's populate is called with its own parent. The root style isn't available at level 3.

    for rel_iter in self.related_populators:

    self.local_setter(from_obj, obj)      # (parent_obj, this_obj)
    if obj is not None:
        self.remote_setter(obj, from_obj)  # (this_obj, parent_obj)
```

    def get_parent_model_select_fields(self, select, klass_info, select_mask):
        """
        Ensure that models that share the parent table with the model selected
        by select_related() also get the parent model columns.
        """
        klass_info["select_fields"] = select_fields = []
        opts = klass_info["model"]._meta
        from_parent = klass_info["from_parent"]
        if not from_parent:
            klass_info["from_parent"] = from_parent = opts.model
        for field in opts.concrete_fields:

            if model == opts.model:

                from_parent
                and model is not None
                and issubclass(from_parent._meta.concrete_model, model._meta.concrete_model)
            ):

```python
def join_parent_model(self, opts, model, alias, seen_models):
    """
    Return the table alias for the given opts. When model is None, return alias
    unmodified. When model's table is already selected, return the existing
    alias (in order to avoid duplicate table aliases)
    """
    if model is None:
        # Base case for inheritance. If there's no model, then use the alias
        # of the joined table.
        return alias
    if not opts or opts.model is not model:
        # There must be a join here. Keep the alias the same as previous (to
        # avoid duplicate table aliases).
        return self.table_alias(model._meta.db_table, create=True)
    # If the parent model has already been seen, return the alias for that
    # model. We don't want to join the parent model more than once.
    if (found_alias := seen_models.get(model)):
        return found_alias
    seen_models[model] = alias
    # It's possible that the alias for this model has already been generated
    # if there's a multi-valued relation in the parent tree.
    if existing_alias := self.query.alias_refcount.get(alias):  # hmm, not exact
        return existing_alias
    return self.table_alias(model._meta.db_table, create=True, ...)?
```

    """
    Used by the ForeignObject field to store information about the relation.

    ``_meta.get_fields()`` returns this class to provide access to the field
    on the related model.

    ``ForeignObjectRel`` objects will be created automatically for
    ``ForeignKey``, ``OneToOneField``, and ``ManyToManyField`` reverse
    relations.

    Users can create ``ForeignObjectRel`` for a generic relation by using
    ``GenericRel`` and specifying it in ``Meta.generic_relations``.
    """

    field_class = None  # Set in ForeignObject.contribute_to_related_class().
    reverse_accessor_name = None
    reverse_related_accessor_name = None
    core_hint = False
    multivalued = None
    on_delete = None
    path_key = None

        field,
        to,
        related_name=None,
        related_query_name=None,
        limit_choices_to=None,

**Implementation:**

In the FR branch of `get_related_selections`:

```python
for name in list(requested):
    # Filtered relations work only on the topmost level.
    if cur_depth > 1:
        break
    if name in self.query._filtered_relations:
        fields_found.add(name)
        (
            final_field,
            _,
            join_opts,
            joins,
            path,
            _,
        ) = self.query.setup_joins([name], opts, root_alias)
        model = join_opts.model
        alias = joins[-1]
        from_parent = (
            issubclass(model, opts.model) and model is not opts.model
        )
        # For multi-hop filtered relations, the local setter must link
        # the leaf to its immediate parent model, not to the root.
        if len(path) == 1:
            local = partial(local_setter, final_field)
        else:
            local = lambda *args: None   # hmm, need a proper no-op
        klass_info = {
            "model": model,
            "field": final_field,
            "reverse": True,
            "local_setter": local,
            "remote_setter": partial(remote_setter, name),
            "from_parent": from_parent,
        }
        related_klass_infos.append(klass_info)
        select_fields = []
        field_select_mask = select_mask.get((name, final_field)) or {}
        columns = self.get_default_columns(
            field_select_mask,
            start_alias=alias,
            opts=model._meta,
            from_parent=opts.model,
        )
        for col in columns:
            select_fields.append(len(select))
            select.append((col, None))
        klass_info["select_fields"] = select_fields
        next_requested = requested.get(name, {})
        next_klass_infos = self.get_related_selections(
            select,
            field_select_mask,
            opts=model._meta,
            root_alias=alias,
            cur_depth=cur_depth + 1,
            requested=next_requested,
            restricted=restricted,
        )
        if len(path) > 1:

```python
class ForeignObjectRel(FieldCacheMixin):
    """
    Used by the ForeignObject field to store information about the relation.

    ``_meta.get_fields()`` returns this class to provide access to the field
    on the related model.

    ``ForeignObjectRel`` objects will be created automatically for
    ``ForeignKey``, ``OneToOneField``, and ``ManyToManyField`` reverse
    relations.

    Users can create ``ForeignObjectRel`` for a generic relation by using
    ``GenericRel`` and specifying it in ``Meta.generic_relations``.
    """

    field_class = None  # Set in ForeignObject.contribute_to_related_class().
    reverse_accessor_name = None
    related_accessor_name = None
    core_hint = False
    multivalued = None
    on_delete = None
    path_key = None

    def __init__(
        self,
        field,
        to,
        related_name=None,
        related_query_name=None,
        limit_choices_to=None,
        parent_link=False,
        on_delete=None,
    ):
        self.field = field
        self.model = to
        self.related_name = related_name
        self.related_query_name = related_query_name
        self.limit_choices_to = {} if limit_choices_to is None else limit_choices_to
        self.parent_link = parent_link
        self.on_delete = on_delete
        self.symmetrical = False

        # This cache is based on the related field. Clear it when the related
        # field name or the related model of the related field change.
        self._cache_name = None
        self._cache_key = (field.name, getattr(field.remote_field, "model", None))
```

def local_setter(final_field, obj, from_obj):
    # Set a reverse fk object when relation is non-empty.
    if from_obj:
        final_field.remote_field.set_cached_value(from_obj, obj)

def remote_setter(name, obj, from_obj):
    setattr(from_obj, name, obj)

for name in list(requested):
    # Filtered relations work only on the topmost level.
    if cur_depth > 1:
        break
    if name in self.query._filtered_relations:
        fields_found.add(name)
        final_field, _, join_opts, joins, _, _ = self.query.setup_joins(
            [name], opts, root_alias
        )
        model = join_opts.model
        alias = joins[-1]
        from_parent = (
            issubclass(model, opts.model) and model is not opts.model
        )
        klass_info = {
            "model": model,
            "field": final_field,
            "reverse": True,
            "local_setter": partial(local_setter, final_field),
            "remote_setter": partial(remote_setter, name),
            "from_parent": from_parent,
        }
        related_klass_infos.append(klass_info)

```python
class ManyToOneRel(ForeignObjectRel):
    """
    Used by the ForeignKey field class to store information about the relation.

    ``related_field`` will be an instance of ForeignKey.

    This object will generally be a member of its parent class, stored in the
    ``rel`` property.
    """

    def __init__(self, field, to, related_name=None, related_query_name=None, limit_choices_to=None, parent_link=False, on_delete=None):
        super().__init__(field, to, related_name=related_name, related_query_name=related_query_name, limit_choices_to=limit_choices_to, parent_link=parent_link, on_delete=on_delete)
        self.symmetrical = False
        self.multiple = True

    @property
    def one_to_many(self):
        return True

    @property
    def one_to_one(self):
        return False

    @property
    def many_to_one(self):
        return not self.multiple

    @property
    def many_to_many(self):
        return False

    @cached_property
    def accessor_name(self):
        ...

    @cached_property
    def reverse_accessor_name(self):
        ...

    @cached_property
    def related_accessor(self):
        return ReverseManyToOneDescriptor(self.field)

    @cached_property
    def reverse_related_accessor(self):
        return self.field.related_accessor

    def get_related_field(self):
        """
        Return the field in the related table that points to the local field.
        """
        model = self.related_model
        if self.related_field is None:
            related_fields = model._meta.private_fields
            for field in related_fields:
                if self.field in field.foreign_related_fields:
                    break
        else:
            field = self.related_field
        if field is None:
            field = model._meta.pk
        return field

    def remove_reverse_hashes(self, instance):
        ...

    def related_query_name(self):
        ...
```

Generally, backward traversal from the leaf: at each step, we're at a model M_k (the to_opts of hop k), and want to link to M_{k-1} (the from_opts of hop k). If hop k is direct (join_field = FK on M_{k-1} pointing to M_k): backward link = reverse FK on M_k → many (or O2O if unique). If hop k is reverse (join_field = rel on M_k pointing to M_{k-1}... wait, reverse hop means M_k has the FK pointing to M_{k-1}): backward link = direct FK on M_k → single ✓.

OK so the general algorithm for the FR branch, walking backward from the leaf:

```
chain = [klass_info_leaf]  # top
prev_model = leaf model (M_n), prev_alias = joins[-1]
for i in range(n-1, 0, -1):  # hops n-1 ... 1 (backward)
    hop = path[i]  # PathInfo from M_i to M_{i+1}; here M_{i+1} == prev_model
    if hop.direct:
        # M_i has the FK to M_{i+1}; backward from M_{i+1} to M_i = reverse rel
        if not unique (i.e., many): break  # cannot select_related
        else: reverse O2O -> klass_info for M_i with field=rel...
    else:
        # M_{i+1} has FK to M_i: single-valued link on M_{i+1}
        fk = hop.join_field.field  # the FK on M_{i+1}
        klass_info for M_i (field=fk, reverse=False, local_setter=fk.set_cached_value)
```

Hmm wait, I have the direction confused. Let me re-define: PathInfo pi_k: from M_k to M_{k+1} (from_opts=M_k, to_opts=M_{k+1}), join_field = field used to join: if direct, FK on M_k pointing to M_{k+1}; if reverse, rel on M_{k+1}... no wait. In Django's PathInfo: `direct=True` means the traversal is via a forward relation (field on from_opts). join_field: for direct, FK on from_opts; for reverse, rel (field on to_opts pointing to from_opts).

```python
    def populate(self, row, from_obj):
        if self.reorder_for_init:
            obj_data = self.reorder_for_init(row)
        else:
            obj_data = row[self.cols_start : self.cols_end]
        if obj_data[self.pk_idx] is None:
            obj = None
        else:
            obj = self.model_cls.from_db(self.db, self.init_list, obj_data)
            for rel_iter in self.related_populators:
                rel_iter.populate(row, obj)
        self.local_setter(from_obj, obj)
        if obj is not None:
            self.remote_setter(obj, from_obj)
```

Let me reconstruct what the actual upstream fix was. The current code (before fix) is:

```python
def local_setter(final_field, obj, from_obj):
    # Set a reverse fk object when relation is non-empty.
    if from_obj:
        final_field.remote_field.set_cached_value(from_obj, obj)

def remote_setter(name, obj, from_obj):
    setattr(from_obj, name, obj)

for name in list(requested):
    # Filtered relations work only on the topmost level.
    if cur_depth > 1:
        break
    if name in self.query._filtered_relations:
        fields_found.add(name)
        final_field, _, join_opts, joins, _, _ = self.query.setup_joins(
            [name], opts, root_alias
        )
        model = join_opts.model
        alias = joins[-1]
        from_parent = (
            issubclass(model, opts.model) and model is not opts.model
        )
        klass_info = {
            "model": model,
            "field": final_field,
            "reverse": True,
            "local_setter": partial(local_setter, final_field),
            "remote_setter": partial(remote_setter, name),
            "from_parent": from_parent,
        }
        related_klass_infos.append(klass_info)
        select_fields = []
        field_select_mask = select_mask.get((name, final_field)) or {}
        columns = self.get_default_columns(
            field_select_mask,
            start_alias=alias,
            opts=model._meta,
            from_parent=opts.model,
        )
        for col in columns:
            select_fields.append(len(select))
            select.append((col, None))
        klass_info["select_fields"] = select_fields
        next_requested = requested.get(name, {})
        next_klass_infos = self.get_related_selections(
            select,
            field_select_mask,
            opts=model._meta,
            root_alias=alias,
            cur_depth=cur_depth + 1,
            requested=next_requested,
            restricted=restricted,
        )
        get_related_klass_infos(klass_info, next_klass_infos)
```

    def populate(self, row, from_obj):
        if self.reorder_for_init:
            obj_data = self.reorder_for_init(row)
        else:
            obj_data = row[self.cols_start : self.cols_end]
        if obj_data[self.pk_idx] is None:
            obj = None
        else:
            obj = self.model_cls.from_db(self.db, self.init_list, obj_data)
            for rel_iter in self.related_populators:
                rel_iter.populate(row, obj)
        self.local_setter(from_obj, obj)
        if obj is not None:
            self.remote_setter(obj, from_obj)

My proposed fix (refined Option A): in the FR branch of `get_related_selections`, after obtaining `final_field, _, join_opts, joins, _, _` — also get the **path** (setup_joins returns 6 values: final_field, targets, join_opts, joins, path, transform). ```python
final_field, _, join_opts, joins, path, _ = self.query.setup_joins([name], opts, root_alias)
```

If the FR is single-hop (len(path) == 1): current behavior (back-cache via final_field.remote_field… wait, for a single-hop, the back-cache is via final_field.remote_field.set_cached_value(leaf, parent)).

Hmm wait, actually, for a single-hop FR where the FR name resolves to a **reverse** relation (e.g., FR('book') where book is a reverse FK name on Author): final_field = ManyToOneRel. final_field.remote_field = forward FK Book.author. set_cached_value(leaf=book, parent=author) → book.author = author ✓ (forward FK cache on leaf — correct!).

For a single-hop FR with a **forward** O2O/FK (e.g. FR('pool') on PoolStyle): final_field = PoolStyle.pool (O2O field). final_field.remote_field = OneToOneRel (reverse, accessor 'poolstyle'). set_cached_value(leaf=pool1, parent=style) → pool1.poolstyle = style ✓.

def get_select_mask(self):
    field_names, defer = self.deferred_loading
    if not field_names:
        return {}
    mask = {}
    for field_name in field_names:
        part_mask = mask
        for part in field_name.split(LOOKUP_SEP):
            part_mask = part_mask.setdefault(part, {})
    opts = self.get_meta()
    if defer:
        return self._get_defer_select_mask(opts, mask)
    return self._get_only_select_mask(opts, mask)
```

```python
def select_related_descend(field, restricted, requested, select_mask, reverse=False):
    """
    Return True if field is select_related and related to the given
    'requested' dict of select_related() lookups, or if it isn't a
    relation, the given 'restricted' set is False (meaning that all
    related models are allowed). 'field' must be a related field.
    """
    if not field.is_relation:
        return not restricted
    if restricted:
        if reverse:
            if not (
                getattr(field.remote_field, "related_query_name", None) in requested
                or getattr(field.remote_field, "related_accessor_name", None) in requested
            ):
                return False
        elif field.name not in requested:
            return False
    select_related = field in select_mask
    select_deferred = (not select_related) and field not in select_mask
    ...
    return select_related or select_deferred  # hmm, roughly
```

Current FR branch code (compiler.py, ~1280-1325):

```python
            def local_setter(final_field, obj, from_obj):
                # Set a reverse fk object when relation is non-empty.
                if from_obj:
                    final_field.remote_field.set_cached_value(from_obj, obj)

            def remote_setter(name, obj, from_obj):
                setattr(from_obj, name, obj)

            for name in list(requested):
                # Filtered relations work only on the topmost level.
                if cur_depth > 1:
                    break
                if name in self.query._filtered_relations:
                    fields_found.add(name)
                    final_field, _, join_opts, joins, _, _ = self.query.setup_joins(
                        [name], opts, root_alias
                    )
                    model = join_opts.model
                    alias = joins[-1]
                    from_parent = (
                        issubclass(model, opts.model) and model is not opts.model
                    )
                    klass_info = {
                        "model": model,
                        "field": final_field,
                        "reverse": True,
                        "local_setter": partial(local_setter, final_field),
                        "remote_setter": partial(remote_setter, name),
                        "from_parent": from_parent,
                    }
                    related_klass_infos.append(klass_info)
                    select_fields = []
                    field_select_mask = select_mask.get((name, final_field)) or {}
                    columns = self.get_default_columns(
                        field_select_mask,
                        start_alias=alias,
                        opts=model._meta,
                        from_parent=opts.model,
                    )
                    for col in columns:
                        select_fields.append(len(select))
                        select.append((col, None))
                    klass_info["select_fields"] = select_fields
                    next_requested = requested.get(name, {})
                    next_klass_infos = self.get_related_selections(
                        select,
                        field_select_mask,
                        opts=model._meta,
                        root_alias=alias,
                        cur_depth=cur_depth + 1,
                        requested=next_requested,
                        restricted=restricted,
                    )
                    get_related_klass_infos(klass_info, next_klass_infos)
```

Let me recall join() in query.py:

```python
    def join(self, join, reuse=None, reuse_with_filtered_relation=False):
        """
        Return an alias for the 'join', either reusing an existing alias for
        that join or creating a new one.

        'join' is a Join object whose parent tables can all re-utilize their
        aliases.
        """
        if reuse_with_filtered_relation and reuse:
            can_reuse = {
                a for i in reuse for a in self.alias_map[:i].tables_chain
            }
        else:
            can_reuse = reuse
        joined_tables = [t for i, t in self.alias_map if i != join.parent_alias]
        reuse_candidate = self._join_plan_optimizable(joined_tables, join, can_reuse)
        if reuse_candidate is not None:
            self.alias_refcounts[reuse_candidate] += 1
            return reuse_candidate
        # If we can not reuse the join, we need to add a new join into the
        # query tree. The find_join_index() method will update the parent
        # alias too, if it has been assigned a placeholder index only.
        target_index = self.find_join_index(join.parent_alias)
        return self._add_join(join, target_index)
```

And `_join_plan_optimizable`: for a direct FK join with no reuse restrictions, if an equivalent join exists (same parent, table, field, join type...), it reuses. The existing tournament join: parent = pool alias (style's pool join — no wait, in our FR query the tournament join's parent is the pool alias, and the FK Pool.tournament). In select_related('pool__tournament'): root's FK branch: setup_joins(['pool'], PoolStyle's opts, root) → pool alias; recursion with root_alias=pool_alias: setup_joins(['tournament'], Pool's opts, pool_alias) → finds existing tournament join (parent=pool_alias) → reuses. So no new join.

   Hmm wait, but more generally: the leaf's parent hop's alias = joins[-2] only if the path has exactly 3 entries and joins has 4 entries (root + 3).    But note: path entries can include parent link hops (model inheritance) which don't add joins? No — all PathInfo entries add joins (setup_joins iterates `for join in path:` and adds each). And names_to_path extends path with path_to_parent entries. So len(joins) == 1 + len(path), generally.

  3. `p[0].pool.tournament` — 1 query

And `p[0].tournament_pool.tournament` should not cause a query, meaning `tournament_pool.tournament` must be cached in the fields_cache of the `tournament_pool` instance, and must be the correct Tournament instance.

The current bug: In the FR branch of `SQLCompiler.get_related_selections`, `final_field` is the last hop's rel (`ManyToOneRel: known_related_objects.pool` — reverse FK from Tournament to Pool). `local_setter` = `partial(local_setter, final_field)` where `local_setter(final_field, obj, from_obj)` executes `final_field.remote_field.set_cached_value(from_obj, obj)` — that is, `final_field.remote_field` is `Pool.tournament` (FK), and `set_cached_value(from_obj=leaf Pool, obj=root PoolStyle)` sets `leaf.tournament = root PoolStyle` — that's the bug! It sets the leaf Pool's `tournament` cache to the root PoolStyle instance.

So `tp._state.fields_cache['tournament']` becomes a PoolStyle instance. That's exactly the corruption.

Actually, let me look at how the existing single-level FR case works: `select_related("pool_1")` with `pool_1=FilteredRelation("pool")`. In this case, the path is PoolStyle -> Pool. final_field = PoolStyle.pool (OneToOneField). local_setter: `final_field.remote_field.set_cached_value(from_obj=Pool, obj=PoolStyle)` — sets `pool.poolstyle = poolstyle` (reverse o2o cache). remote_setter: `setattr(poolstyle, 'pool_1', pool)`. This works.

Multi-level FR: path PoolStyle -> Pool -> Tournament -> Pool. final_field = ManyToOneRel (Tournament's reverse pool). local_setter sets `final_field.remote_field.set_cached_value(from_obj, obj)` = `Pool.tournament.set_cached_value(leaf_pool, poolstyle)` — wrong, because the local model of the rel is Tournament, not PoolStyle! For a single-level FR where relation_name is like "pool" (FK target), the last hop is direct (PoolStyle.pool) and `final_field` is the FK itself, so `final_field.remote_field.set_cached_value(from_obj=Pool, obj=PoolStyle)` is correct.

But for multi-level, the last hop might be a reverse FK, and its local model (Tournament) is an intermediate model, not the root. So `from_obj` (the root PoolStyle) is wrong for that cache.

So the fix is: for a multi-level FR, we shouldn't try to set the "reverse cache" on the leaf at all — because the intermediate model (Tournament) isn't an instance being populated. Instead, what should happen?

Option A: Set the FK cache on the leaf: `tp.tournament_id` is available but `tp.tournament` instance isn't. We can't cache an instance without an instance.

```python
def get_default_columns(self, select_mask, start_alias=None, opts=None, from_parent=None):
    result = []
    if opts is None:
        if (opts := self.query.get_meta()) is None:
            return result
    start_alias = start_alias or self.query.get_initial_alias()
    seen_models = {None: start_alias}
    for field in opts.concrete_fields:
        model = field.model._meta.concrete_model
        if model == opts.model:
            model = None
        if (
            from_parent
            and model is not None
            and issubclass(
                from_parent._meta.concrete_model, model._meta.concrete_model
            )
        ):
            continue
        if select_mask and field not in select_mask:
            continue
        alias = self.query.join_parent_model(opts, model, start_alias, seen_models)
        column = field.get_col(alias)
        result.append(column)
    return result
```

Hmm wait — `select_mask` here is `field_select_mask` = `select_mask.get((name, final_field)) or {}` = {} → falsy → no skip. Tournament has 2 concrete fields → 2 columns. start_alias = joins[-2] = tournament table alias...

Ahhhh wait!!! I think I've got it. **`self.query.join_parent_model`** — no wait. Let me look at `seen_models = {None: start_alias}` and `alias = self.query.join_parent_model(opts, model, start_alias, seen_models)`:

```python
def join_parent_model(self, child_opts, parent_model, start_alias, seen_models):
    """
    Ensure a proper join to the given child_opts. If start_alias points to
    an intermediate table, then start_alias is remapped to the parent model
    table. Used for model inheritance cases.
    """
```

I need the body. If parent_model is None → probably returns seen_models.get(None, start_alias) = start_alias. No problem.

Hmm, actually ForeignObjectRel inherits FieldCacheMixin:

```python
class FieldCacheMixin:
    def set_cached_value(self, instance, value):
        instance._state.fields_cache[
            self.get_cache_name()
        ] = value

    def get_cached_value(self, instance, default=SENTINEL):
        cache_name = self.get_cache_name()
        try:
            return instance._state.fields_cache[cache_name]
        except KeyError:
            pass
        return default

    def is_cached(self, instance):
        return self.get_cache_name() in instance._state.fields_cache
```

And `ManyToOneRel.get_cache_name()` = `get_accessor_name()`. Hmm wait, for a ManyToOneRel (reverse of Pool.tournament on Tournament), `get_accessor_name()` = related_name or model_name + '_set'/''. If the reverse is many (FK), multiple=True → 'pool_set'… so ManyToOneRel.set_cached_value would set `tournament._state.fields_cache['pool_set'] = pool`?? That's not even a real cache name — the reverse accessor is a manager/descriptor and isn't usually cached in fields_cache… but the code just sets it. Hmm, this could be harmful but mostly harmless (fields_cache['pool_set'] wouldn't be read by the descriptor… actually would it?     def get_field(self, field_name):
        """
        Return a field instance given the name of a forward or reverse field.
        """
        try:
            # In order to avoid premature loading of the relation field
            # (the *descriptors* ForeignKey and OneToOneField),
            # return the object from the local-dict.
            return self.fields_map[field_name]
        except KeyError:
            # If the FK field is cached, return it from the cache.
            if field_name in self._relation_cache:
                return self._relation_cache[field_name]
        for field in self.related_objects:
            ...
```

    def set_cached_value(self, instance, value):
        instance._state.fields_cache[self.get_cache_name()] = value

Hmm, no. Let me recall FieldCacheMixin (in django/db/models/fields/mixins.py):

```python
class FieldCacheMixin:
    """
    Provide the cached lookups functionality.

    This mixin defines a cache attribute to be used by get_cached_value()
    and set_cached_value().

    In order to use set_cached_value(), a Field instance must be
    aware of the accessor that defines how to retrieve the relation from the
    target field. That's why this mixin is required for the following cases:
    1) Forward FK/M2M accesses;
    2) Reverse O2O/FK accesses;
    3) Forward or reverse M2M accesses through the intermediate
    'through' model.
    """

    # Attribute used by the get_cached_value() method.
    cache_name = None
    # Attribute used by the set_cached_value() method.
    cache_setter = None

    def __init__(self):
        self.cache_name = None
        self.cache_setter = None

    def __getstate__(self):
        state = super().__getstate__()
        state.pop("cache_name", None)
        state.pop("cache_setter", None)
        return state

    def get_cached_value(self, instance, default=empty):
        return instance._state.fields_cache.get(self.cache_name, default)

    def set_cached_value(self, instance, value):
        if self.cache_setter:
            self.cache_setter(instance, value)
        instance._state.fields_cache[self.cache_name] = value
```

And ForeignObjectRel:

```python
    def __init__(self, ...):
        ...
        self.symmetrical = False
        self.multiple = True
        self.field_name = None
        ...
    ...
    def contribute_to_related_class(self, related_class):
        ...

```python
if last_hop.direct:
    f = last_hop.join_field  # FK/O2O on B pointing to C
    if f.unique:
        def intermediate_remote_setter(b, c):
            f.set_cached_value(b, c)
            f.remote_field.set_cached_value(c, b)
    else:
        intermediate_remote_setter = lambda b, c: f.set_cached_value(b, c)
    intermediate_local_setter = lambda b, c: None
else:
    g = last_hop.join_field.remote_field  # FK/O2O on C pointing to B
    if g.unique:

            g.remote_field.set_cached_value(b, c)

        intermediate_remote_setter = lambda b, c: None
    intermediate_local_setter = g.set_cached_value
```

Let me approach this from first principles, since I've already deeply traced the bug, and try to remember the upstream fix.

The bug: for a multi-level FilteredRelation, the final join hop (Tournament -> Pool reverse FK) is the same as the "last hop" of the FR's relation_name. The FR branch in `get_related_selections` treats the whole thing like a single reverse FK from root to leaf model: `klass_info["field"] = final_field` (ManyToOneRel Tournament.pool), `local_setter` = `partial(local_setter, final_field)` where `local_setter(final_field, obj, from_obj)` does `final_field.remote_field.set_cached_value(from_obj, obj)`.

Wait, actually I need to check the argument mapping in RelatedPopulator.populate():

```python
    def populate(self, row, from_obj):
        ...
        self.local_setter(from_obj, obj)
        if obj is not None:
            self.remote_setter(obj, from_obj)
```

So `local_setter(from_obj, obj)`: in the partial, `partial(local_setter, final_field)` is called with (from_obj, obj) → `local_setter(final_field, from_obj, obj)`, i.e. `final_field=final_field, obj=from_obj (parent/root instance), from_obj=obj (leaf instance)`. And the body: `final_field.remote_field.set_cached_value(from_obj, obj)` → `set_cached_value(leaf, root)`.

For a single-level FR like `PoolStyle.annotate(pool_1=FilteredRelation("pool")).select_related("pool_1")`: final_field is the reverse OneToOneRel of PoolStyle.pool (Pool -> PoolStyle.pool). `final_field.remote_field` is the OneToOneField PoolStyle.pool itself. `set_cached_value(leaf=pool, obj=poolstyle)` → `pool.poolstyle = poolstyle` — correct! And `remote_setter(name, obj, from_obj)` → `setattr(from_obj=poolstyle, name, leaf=pool)` → `poolstyle.pool_1 = pool` — correct.

For a multi-level FR: final_field = ManyToOneRel (Tournament.pool). `final_field.remote_field` = Pool.tournament FK. `local_setter` does `Pool.tournament.set_cached_value(leaf_pool, poolstyle)` → `leaf_pool.tournament = poolstyle` — wrong (corruption).

And `remote_setter` does `setattr(poolstyle, 'tournament_pool', leaf_pool)` — actually this is fine.

So the minimal fix: for a multi-level FR, don't use the FK's remote_field setter as local_setter. Instead, we should set the relation that actually connects the leaf to the rest of the path, which is the last hop: Tournament --reverse FK--> Pool. Hmm, but wait — what does the test actually require?

Test:
```python
with self.assertNumQueries(3):
    p = list(qs)
    self.assertEqual(p[0].pool.tournament, p[0].tournament_pool.tournament)
```

Accesses:

Actually the exact code is:

```python
def select_related_descend(field, restricted, requested, select_mask, reverse=False):
    """
    Determine whether a field should be selected through by select_related().
    This is controlled by the "select_mask" which restricts the traversal
    through the relation graph.
    """
    # reverse (i.e., field is on the related model but we're trying to
    # see if we should include it from the other side), or
    # if the field is not a relation
    if reverse or not field.is_relation:
        return False
    if restricted:
        # if this path isn't requested, we don't descend
        if not (requested.get(field.name, {}) or field.name in requested):
            return False
    ...
```

Let me look at the actual code (from the repo):

```python
def select_related_descend(field, restricted, requested, select_mask, reverse=False):
    """
    Determine whether a field should be selected through by select_related().
    This is controlled by the "select_mask" which restricts the traversal
    through the relation graph.
    """
    # reverse (i.e., field is on the related model but we're trying to
    # see if we should include it from the other side), or
    # the field is not a relation
    if reverse or not field.is_relation:
        return False
    if restricted:
        # if this path isn't requested, we don't descend
        if not requested.get(field.name, {}):
            return False
    # ...
```

def populate(self, row, from_obj):
    if self.reorder_for_init:
        obj_data = self.reorder_for_init(row)
    else:
        obj_data = row[self.cols_start : self.cols_end]

        obj = None
    else:
        obj = self.model_cls.from_db(self.db, self.init_list, obj_data)

Let me check select_related_descend(f, restricted, requested, select_mask):

```python
def select_related_descend(field, restricted, requested, select_mask, reverse=False):
    """
    Check if a field can be used with select_related().
    ...
    """
    if field.is_relation and not field.many_to_many and field.related_model:
        if restricted:
            names = requested
            rel_reverse_name = field.remote_field.related_query_name()
            rel_name = field.name
            if reverse:
                rel_reverse_name, rel_name = rel_name, rel_reverse_name
            return (
                (rel_name in names and names[rel_name])
                or (rel_reverse_name in names and names[rel_reverse_name])
            )
        else:
            return True
    return False
```

So pool (O2O): restricted → 'pool' not in requested → False. So the pool join isn't auto-selected... but wait — `select_related('pool')` in a test like test_one_to_one_select_related works because 'pool' is in requested. OK.

```python
def populate(self, row, from_obj):
    ...

So for a related klass_info K that is a child of the root:
- `local_setter(from_obj=root_obj, obj=K_obj)` — sets something on the **root** (from_obj) about K.
- `remote_setter(obj=K_obj, from_obj=root_obj)` — sets something on K_obj about the root.

```python
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/testbed/tests')
import django
from django.conf import settings
settings.configure(DEBUG=True,
    DATABASES={'default': {'ENGINE': 'django.db.backends.sqlite3', 'NAME': ':memory:'}},
    INSTALLED_APPS=['known_related_objects'])
django.setup()
from django.db import connection
from django.db.models import FilteredRelation
from django.test.utils import CaptureQueriesContext
from known_related_objects.models import Organiser, Pool, PoolStyle, Tournament

with connection.schema_editor() as se:
    for m in (Tournament, Organiser, Pool, PoolStyle):
        se.create_model(m)
t1 = Tournament.objects.create(name="Tourney 1"); t2 = Tournament.objects.create(name="Tourney 2")
o1 = Organiser.objects.create(name="Organiser 1")
p1 = Pool.objects.create(name="T1 Pool 1", tournament=t1, organiser=o1)
p2 = Pool.objects.create(name="T1 Pool 2", tournament=t1, organiser=o1)
p3 = Pool.objects.create(name="T2 Pool 1", tournament=t2, organiser=o1)
p4 = Pool.objects.create(name="T2 Pool 2", tournament=t2, organiser=o1)
ps1 = PoolStyle.objects.create(name="T1 Pool 2 Style", pool=p2)
ps2 = PoolStyle.objects.create(name="T2 Pool 1 Style", pool=p3)
ps3 = PoolStyle.objects.create(name="T1 Pool 1/3 Style", pool=p1, another_pool=p3)

# 1) issue scenario
qs = PoolStyle.objects.annotate(tournament_pool=FilteredRelation('pool__tournament__pool')).select_related('tournament_pool')
with CaptureQueriesContext(connection) as ctx:
    p = list(qs)
    a = p[0].pool.tournament
    b = p[0].tournament_pool.tournament
assert a == b, (a, b)
assert len(ctx.captured_queries) == 3, len(ctx.captured_queries)
print("scenario1 OK: 3 queries, equality")

# 2) new test scenario: FR pool__another_style from Tournament
qs2 = Tournament.objects.annotate(style=FilteredRelation('pool__another_style')).select_related('style').filter(pk=t2.pk)
sql2 = str(qs2.query)
print("SQL2:", sql2)
assert '"known_related_objects_pool".id' in sql2  # intermediate columns selected
with CaptureQueriesContext(connection) as ctx2:
    rows = list(qs2)
    row = next(r for r in rows if r.style is not None)
    s = row.style
    p = s.another_pool          # cached (A), no query
    x = p.another_style         # NOT cached (B), 1 query
assert s is ps3
assert p is p3
assert x is s

```python
@classmethod
def from_db(cls, db, field_names, values):
    if len(values) != len(cls._meta.concrete_fields):
        values_iter = iter(values)
        values = [next(values_iter) if f.attname in field_names else DEFERRED for f in cls._meta.concrete_fields]
    new = cls(*values)
    new._state.adding = False
    new._state.db = db
    return new
```

No cache. OK.

```python
class ReverseOneToOneDescriptor:
    def __get__(self, instance, cls=None):
        if instance is None:
            return self

        try:
            rel_obj = self.get_related(instance)
        except self.related.model.DoesNotExist:
            rel_obj = None

        # Populates the forward cache of the one-to-one relation
        setattr(instance, self.cache_name, rel_obj)
        return rel_obj
```
